rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **dot product** a·b = |a||b|cos θ = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃ turns two vectors into one number — an **agreement meter**: +|a||b| when aligned, 0 when perpendicular, negative when opposed. Its algebra is commutative and distributive but has **no cancellation**; its geometry gives the theorems: **a ⊥ b ⟺ a·b = 0**, **cos θ = a·b/(|a||b|)**, and the **projection** family — scalar projection a·b/|b| (signed shadow) and…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
a·b = |a||b|cos θ = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃; |a| = √(a·a)
a ⊥ b ⟺ a·b = 0; cos θ = a·b/(|a||b|)
scalar projection of a on b: a·b/|b|; vector projection: (a·b/|b|²)b

rows.text: Verified PYQs: NEB 2024 (a.b = -3; scalar projection 4/sqrt5; angle 60 degrees), NEB 2023 (MCQ -8/3) — assigned to this row.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "a perp b iff a.b = 0 (non-zero vectors); cos th = a.b/(|a||b|); scalar projection of a on b = a.b/|b|."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The signed shadow*** — scalar projection is a's shadow on b's line, and shadows can fall backwards: negative projection means the angle is obtuse.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The dot product is an agreement meter: cos th rewards alignment, punishes opposition, and stays silent at right angles.  ·  Dot product: a.b = |a||b| cos th = a1b1 + a2b2 + a3b3. a.a = |a|^2. Laws: commutative, distributive, scalar associative; NO cancellation. Perpendicularity theorem: a perp b (non-zero) iff a.b = 0. Angle theorem: cos th = a.b/(|a||b|). Scalar projection of a on b: a.b/|b| (signed); vector projection: (a.b/|b|^2) b. i, j, k orthonormal: self products 1, cross products 0.…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Projection Machine The **dot (scalar) product** a·b = |a||b|cos θ multiplies two vectors into a scalar. Its theorems: commutativity, distributivity over addition, perpendicularity criterion a·b = 0, and the **projection** interpretation — the dot product is "how much of a lies along b".  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Definition and component form - **a·b = |a||b| cos θ**, 0 ≤ θ ≤ π. - **Component form:** a·b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃a₃... i.e. a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃ (from î·î = ĵ·ĵ = k̂·k̂ = 1 and mixed products 0). - **a·a = |a|²** — magnitude from the dot product: |a| = √(a·a). ### 2.2 Algebraic laws - **Commutative:** a·b = b·a (cos θ is even). - **Distributive:** a·(b + c) = a·b + a·c.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Component multiply-and-add. |a| = sqrt(a.a). Perpendicular iff dot = 0. Projection: dot divided by |b|. Angle: dot over product of magnitudes, then compare with standard cosines.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): If a = 2î + 3ĵ − k̂ and b = î − ĵ + 2k̂, find a·b. (3m with |a×b|)** — **Component form:** a·b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃ = (2)(1) + (3)(−1) + (−1)(2) = 2 − 3 − 2 = **−3**. **Interpretation:** the negative dot product means cos θ < 0 — the angle between the vectors is **obtuse** (between 90° and 180°).…  ·  **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): The scalar projection of the vector a = (2, −1, 4) on the vector b = (1, 2, −2) is: (1m)** — **Dot product:** a·b = (2)(1) + (−1)(2) + (4)(−2) = 2 − 2 − 8 = −8. **Magnitude of b:** |b| = √(1² + 2² + (−2)²) = √9 = 3. **Scalar projection:** a·b/|b| = **−8/3 — option (a)**.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For angle questions, finish with the degree/radian value — cos th = 1/2 alone is half the answer.

rows.text: Work = F.d is the dot product's day job: only the force component along the motion earns energy.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Find the angle between a = î + ĵ and b = ĵ + k̂. (2m)** — **Dot product:** a·b = (1)(0) + (1)(1) + (0)(1) = 1. **Magnitudes:** |a| = √(1 + 1) = √2; |b| = √(1 + 1) = √2. **Angle theorem:** cos θ = a·b/(|a||b|) = 1/(√2·√2) = 1/2.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **a·b = 0 needs non-zero vectors:** the zero vector is perpendicular to everything by convention — state the non-zero hypothesis in proofs.  ·  **Projection divides by |b|, not |b|²:** scalar projection a·b/|b|; the vector projection is the one carrying |b|².  ·  **No cancellation law:** from a·b = a·c conclude a·(b − c) = 0 (b − c ⊥ a), never b = c.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 7. Exam Application **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): If a = 2î + 3ĵ − k̂ and b = î − ĵ + 2k̂, find a·b. (part of 3m)** — **a·b = (2)(1) + (3)(−1) + (−1)(2) = 2 − 3 − 2 = −3.** The negative sign says the angle between the vectors is obtuse (cos θ < 0).  ·  **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Find the scalar projection of a = 2î + ĵ on b = î + 2ĵ. (3m)** — **a·b** = (2)(1) + (1)(2) = 4; **|b|** = √(1 + 4) = √5. **Scalar projection = a·b/|b| = 4/√5** = 4√5/5 ≈ 1.79. (Positive ⟹ the projection points along b.)  ·  **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): The scalar projection of a = (2, −1, 4) on b = (1, 2, −2) is: (1m MCQ)** — a·b = 2 − 2 − 8 = −8; |b| = √(1 + 4 + 4) = 3; projection = **−8/3 → option (a)**. The negative value flags an obtuse angle between the vectors.
